titleEn: I Want to Carry It on My Head, Too!

pages.text: The river had dropped far down. Fetching water meant walking a long way down the steps. Raju, the eldest child, came up with a big jar on their head.
Mina, the middle child, wanted to bring water that way, too. "I want to carry it on my head!" Sonu, the youngest, watched beside Mina.
Mom offered a small jar. "How about this?" Mina hugged a big jar just like Raju's.
At the bottom of the steps, Mina filled it to the top. The jar was heavy.
Mina climbed with it on their head. One step, two, three. Their arms trembled.
Sitting on a step to rest, Mina tipped sideways. Splash! Water poured over the steps.
Only a handspan of water remained. Mina looked inside. The steps stretched far above.
Mom came down with water in a small jar. She gently set it on Mina's head. "Let's try this one."
The small jar was light. After one trip, Mina fetched water again and came up. "Mom, I brought another load!"
The house's water jar filled with sloshing water. Mom tapped it. "Today's rice will be cooked with Mina's water."
